name: Digestive system
description: The digestive tract and its accessory organs: the digestive tract as a whole, the mouth, teeth and oesophagus, the stomach, the small and large intestine, the liver, gallbladder, pancreas and spleen, and how food is broken down and absorbed. Picture questions show the organs, drawn see-through inside the trunk, with one highlighted to name.

source.name: Written for Study Buddy. Pictures rendered from BodyParts3D (© The Database Center for Life Science, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP).

questions.prompt: In order, what are the main parts of the digestive tract?
answers: Mouth, pharynx, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, anus
Mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, anus
wrong: Mouth, oesophagus, pharynx, stomach, large intestine, small intestine, anus
Mouth, pharynx, stomach, oesophagus, small intestine, large intestine, anus
Mouth, pharynx, oesophagus, small intestine, stomach, large intestine, anus
questions.explanation: About 9 metres from mouth to anus. The liver, gallbladder and pancreas are accessory organs: food does not pass through them.

figure.alt: The whole digestive tract inside the trunk, in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the six jobs of the digestive system?
answers: Ingestion, propulsion, mechanical digestion, chemical digestion, absorption and defaecation
Ingestion, propulsion, mechanical and chemical digestion, absorption, defecation
wrong: Ingestion, respiration, digestion, excretion, secretion and circulation
Intake, storage, filtering, absorption, synthesis and elimination
Ingestion, absorption, filtration, secretion, reabsorption and excretion

questions.prompt: Which three organs add secretions to the digestive tract but never have food pass through them?
questions.explanation: Together with the salivary glands, they are the accessory digestive organs.

questions.prompt: From the lumen outwards, what are the four layers of the wall of the digestive tract?
questions.explanation: The mucosa lines the tube, the submucosa carries vessels and nerves, the muscularis externa has the circular and longitudinal muscle, and the serosa (the visceral peritoneum) is the outer covering.

questions.prompt: What is the wave of muscle contraction that pushes food along the digestive tract called?
questions.explanation: Circular muscle tightens behind the food and the longitudinal muscle shortens the tube ahead of it.

questions.prompt: What kind of movement of the small intestine mixes the chyme with digestive juices without moving it on?
questions.explanation: Rings of contraction chop the contents back and forth.

questions.prompt: Which network of nerves in the wall of the gut controls its movements and secretions?
questions.explanation: The myenteric (Auerbach's) plexus controls movement; the submucosal (Meissner's) plexus controls secretion.

questions.prompt: What is the thin membrane lining the abdominal cavity and covering the organs called?
questions.explanation: The parietal layer lines the wall; the visceral layer covers the organs. Between them is the peritoneal cavity, with a little fluid.

questions.prompt: What fold of peritoneum attaches the small intestine to the back wall of the abdomen and carries its blood vessels?
questions.explanation: Long enough to let the small intestine move.

questions.prompt: What is the large apron-like fold of peritoneum hanging down from the stomach over the intestines called?
questions.explanation: Nicknamed the 'policeman of the abdomen' because it wraps round inflamed areas.

questions.prompt: Which of these organs lies behind the peritoneum (retroperitoneal)?
questions.explanation: Also the kidneys, most of the duodenum, the ascending and descending colon and the aorta.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme in saliva begins the digestion of starch?
questions.explanation: It breaks starch into smaller sugars; you can taste this if you chew a cracker for a while.

questions.prompt: What are the three pairs of large salivary glands?
questions.explanation: The parotid, in front of the ear, is the largest. Mumps is an infection of it.

questions.prompt: Mumps is a viral infection of which gland?
How many permanent teeth does an adult usually have, including wisdom teeth?
questions.explanation: Eight incisors, four canines, eight premolars and 12 molars.

figure.alt: The skull and jaw, with all of the teeth in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: How many milk (deciduous) teeth does a child have?
questions.explanation: There are no premolars in the milk set: just incisors, canines and molars.

questions.prompt: What are the four types of permanent teeth, from the front of the mouth to the back?
questions.explanation: Incisors cut, canines tear, premolars and molars grind.

questions.prompt: Which teeth are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The eight chisel-shaped front teeth, for cutting.

figure.alt: The skull and jaw, with some teeth in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which teeth are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The four pointed teeth, one each side of the incisors, for tearing.

figure.alt: The skull and jaw, with some teeth in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which teeth are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Eight teeth with two cusps each, between the canines and molars.

figure.alt: The skull and jaw, with some teeth in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which teeth are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The big back teeth, with three to five cusps, for grinding. The third molars are the wisdom teeth.

figure.alt: The skull and jaw, with some teeth in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the hardest substance in the body, covering the crown of a tooth?
questions.explanation: About 96% mineral, mostly hydroxyapatite. It cannot regrow once lost.

questions.prompt: What is the bone-like tissue that makes up most of a tooth, under the enamel, called?
questions.explanation: It is softer than enamel and has tiny tubules, which is why exposed dentine is sensitive.

questions.prompt: What is the soft centre of a tooth, holding its nerves and blood vessels, called?
questions.explanation: Toothache comes from inflamed pulp.

questions.prompt: What holds a tooth in its socket?
questions.explanation: A fibrous joint (a gomphosis) between the cementum of the root and the bone of the socket.

questions.prompt: Which phase of swallowing can you control voluntarily?
questions.explanation: The pharyngeal and oesophageal phases are automatic reflexes.

questions.prompt: During swallowing, what stops food going into the windpipe?
answers: The larynx rises and the epiglottis covers its entrance
The epiglottis closes over the larynx
questions.explanation: Breathing stops briefly at the same time.

questions.prompt: Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The muscular tube, about 25 cm long, taking food from the pharynx to the stomach behind the windpipe and heart.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: About how long is the oesophagus?
questions.explanation: From the level of C6 to T11. It runs through the diaphragm at T10.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with the oesophagus in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What kind of muscle makes up the walls of the oesophagus?
answers: Skeletal at the top, smooth at the bottom
Skeletal in the upper third and smooth in the lower third
questions.explanation: The middle third has a mix.

questions.prompt: What keeps stomach acid from flowing back up into the oesophagus?
questions.explanation: When it is weak, acid reflux and heartburn (GORD) result.

questions.prompt: What is it called when part of the stomach pushes up through the diaphragm into the chest?
Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The J-shaped bag under the left side of the diaphragm, just below the oesophagus.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the main parts of the stomach, from the oesophagus to the small intestine?
questions.explanation: The fundus is the dome that sits above the entrance of the oesophagus; the pylorus is the narrow outlet.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with the stomach in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the folds in the lining of the empty stomach called?
questions.explanation: They flatten as the stomach fills; it can hold 1.5 litres or more.

questions.prompt: Which cells of the stomach lining make hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: They also make intrinsic factor, needed to absorb vitamin B12.

questions.prompt: Which cells of the stomach lining make pepsinogen, the inactive form of the protein-digesting enzyme pepsin?
questions.explanation: Acid turns it into active pepsin.

questions.prompt: About what is the pH of the stomach's contents?
questions.explanation: Strongly acid, which kills most bacteria and starts protein digestion.

questions.prompt: What protects the stomach wall from its own acid and pepsin?
answers: A thick layer of alkaline mucus
questions.explanation: Aspirin and the bacterium Helicobacter pylori damage it, causing ulcers.

questions.prompt: Which bacterium is the main cause of stomach ulcers?
questions.explanation: Treated with antibiotics and acid suppression.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin needs a stomach protein called intrinsic factor for its absorption?
questions.explanation: Without it a person gets pernicious anaemia.

questions.prompt: Which hormone, made by G cells of the stomach, makes it secrete acid?
Which hormone from the stomach stimulates hunger?
questions.explanation: Levels rise before meals and fall after eating.

questions.prompt: What is the semi-liquid mixture of food and gastric juice leaving the stomach called?
questions.explanation: The bolus is the ball of chewed food that is swallowed.

questions.prompt: What controls the passage of chyme from the stomach into the duodenum?
Which type of food slows stomach emptying most?
questions.explanation: Fat in the duodenum triggers hormones (such as CCK) that delay emptying, which is why a fatty meal feels heavy.

questions.prompt: Which part of the brain controls vomiting?
Which artery gives the stomach most of its blood?
questions.explanation: Branches of the celiac trunk supply it.

questions.prompt: Which part of the digestive tract is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The coiled tube filling the middle of the abdomen. About 6 m long when relaxed.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the three parts of the small intestine, in order?
questions.explanation: The jejunum makes up about two fifths, the ileum three fifths of the length beyond the duodenum.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with the small intestine in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The first 25 cm of the small intestine, curved like a C round the head of the pancreas. Pancreatic juice and bile enter it.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part of the small intestine receives bile and pancreatic juice?
questions.explanation: Through the hepatopancreatic ampulla (of Vater), opening at the major duodenal papilla.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with the duodenum in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The middle part, mostly in the upper left of the abdomen. It is where most absorption happens.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The last and longest part, mostly in the lower right of the abdomen, ending at the ileocaecal valve.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which vitamin is absorbed only in the last part of the ileum, along with bile salts?
questions.explanation: Surgery or Crohn's disease in the ileum can cause B12 deficiency.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with the ileum in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the finger-like projections of the small intestine's lining that increase its surface area called?
questions.explanation: Each has a capillary network and a lymph vessel (lacteal).

questions.prompt: What do we call the tiny projections on the surface of the cells covering each villus, forming the 'brush border'?
questions.explanation: The brush border also holds enzymes such as lactase and maltase.

questions.prompt: What are the permanent circular folds of the small intestine's lining called?
questions.explanation: Plicae, villi and microvilli together make a surface of about 200 square metres.

questions.prompt: What is the lymph vessel in the centre of each villus, which absorbs fats, called?
questions.explanation: Fats go into the lymph as chylomicrons, not directly into the blood.

questions.prompt: What are the pits between villi, where the lining cells are renewed, called?
questions.explanation: The lining is replaced every few days.

questions.prompt: Which glands in the duodenum make alkaline mucus to protect it from stomach acid?
What are the clusters of lymphoid tissue in the wall of the ileum called?
questions.explanation: They watch for bacteria and viruses in the gut.

questions.prompt: Which hormone from the duodenum makes the gallbladder contract and the pancreas release enzymes?
Which hormone from the duodenum makes the pancreas release bicarbonate to neutralise the acid from the stomach?
questions.explanation: The first hormone ever discovered (1902).

questions.prompt: Where does most absorption of nutrients take place?
questions.explanation: Nearly all nutrients, 90% of the water and the vitamins B and C; the large intestine takes the rest of the water.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme in the brush border digests the milk sugar lactose?
questions.explanation: Without it, lactose reaches the colon and is fermented, causing wind and diarrhoea (lactose intolerance).

questions.prompt: In coeliac disease the immune system damages the villi in reaction to which protein?
questions.explanation: Gluten is in wheat, barley and rye.

questions.prompt: What valve stops the contents of the large intestine from going back into the ileum?
Which part of the digestive tract is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The wide tube framing the small intestine: ascending, transverse, descending and sigmoid parts. About 1.5 m long.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: In order from the caecum, what are the parts of the large intestine?
answers: Caecum, ascending colon, transverse colon, descending colon, sigmoid colon, rectum, anal canal
Cecum, ascending colon, transverse colon, descending colon, sigmoid colon, rectum, anal canal
wrong: Caecum, descending colon, transverse colon, ascending colon, sigmoid colon, rectum, anal canal
Caecum, ascending colon, descending colon, transverse colon, sigmoid colon, rectum, anal canal
Caecum, transverse colon, ascending colon, sigmoid colon, descending colon, rectum, anal canal
questions.explanation: It rises on the right, crosses to the left and goes down.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with the colon in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the pouches of the colon wall called?
questions.explanation: They're made by the taeniae coli pulling the wall into sacs.

questions.prompt: What are the three bands of longitudinal muscle on the outside of the colon called?
questions.explanation: They're shorter than the gut, which gathers it into haustra.

questions.prompt: What is the main job of the large intestine?
answers: To absorb water and salts and form faeces
questions.explanation: About 1.5 litres of fluid reach it each day and all but 100 mL is absorbed.

questions.prompt: What do the bacteria in the large intestine make that we absorb?
answers: Vitamin K and some B vitamins
questions.explanation: They also ferment fibre into short-chain fatty acids that feed the colon wall.

questions.prompt: What makes the colour of normal faeces?
questions.explanation: Stercobilin comes from the breakdown of bilirubin by gut bacteria. Pale faeces suggest that bile isn't getting to the gut.

questions.prompt: Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A narrow, blind-ended tube off the caecum, in the lower right of the abdomen.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Pain in the lower right of the abdomen, usually starting near the navel, is the classic sign of inflammation of which organ?
questions.explanation: McBurney's point, a third of the way from the right anterior superior iliac spine to the navel, is the usual place of the tenderness.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with the appendix in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The last 12 to 15 cm of the large intestine, in front of the sacrum.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which two sphincters close the anal canal?
answers: The internal and external anal sphincters
questions.explanation: The internal one is smooth muscle (involuntary); the external is skeletal muscle (voluntary).

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with the rectum in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What triggers the urge to defecate?
What are small pouches that bulge out of the wall of the colon called?
questions.explanation: They are common over 60. If inflamed, it's diverticulitis.

questions.prompt: Which two diseases make up inflammatory bowel disease?
questions.explanation: Crohn's can affect any part of the gut; ulcerative colitis affects only the colon and rectum.

questions.prompt: Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The largest internal organ, under the right side of the diaphragm.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: About how much does the adult liver weigh?
questions.explanation: It's the largest gland in the body and holds about 13% of the blood.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with the liver in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the four lobes of the liver?
questions.explanation: The falciform ligament separates the right and left lobes on the front.

questions.prompt: The liver gets blood from which two vessels?
answers: The hepatic artery and the hepatic portal vein
wrong: The hepatic artery and the inferior vena cava
The portal vein and the hepatic vein
questions.explanation: About 75% comes from the portal vein (nutrient-rich), 25% from the hepatic artery (oxygen-rich).

questions.prompt: Where does blood leave the liver?
answers: Through the hepatic veins into the inferior vena cava
Hepatic veins to the inferior vena cava
wrong: Through the portal vein to the heart

questions.prompt: What is the main cell of the liver called?
Which cells in the liver sinusoids engulf old red blood cells and bacteria?
What is the six-sided functional unit of the liver, with a central vein at its middle, called?
questions.explanation: Portal triads (a branch each of the portal vein, hepatic artery and bile duct) sit at its corners.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a function of the liver?
questions.explanation: Insulin comes from the beta cells of the pancreas. The liver does store glycogen and respond to insulin.

questions.prompt: What is the main job of bile?
questions.explanation: Bile salts break large fat drops into small ones, giving lipase more surface to work on. Bile has no enzymes.

questions.prompt: What yellow pigment from the breakdown of haemoglobin, removed by the liver in bile, builds up in jaundice?
questions.explanation: Jaundice is the yellowing of the skin and the whites of the eyes.

questions.prompt: What is yellowing of the skin and eyes from raised bilirubin called?
What is inflammation of the liver called?
questions.explanation: Often from viruses (A, B, C), alcohol or drugs.

questions.prompt: What is the replacement of liver tissue by scar tissue, which blocks blood flow through it, called?
questions.explanation: Common causes are alcohol, hepatitis B and C and fatty liver disease.

questions.prompt: In cirrhosis, raised pressure in the portal vein can cause swollen veins at the lower end of the oesophagus. What are they called?
questions.explanation: They can burst and bleed heavily.

questions.prompt: What is unusual about the liver's response to damage?
questions.explanation: A person can lose up to two thirds of it and it regrows within weeks.

questions.prompt: Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A small pear-shaped bag tucked under the liver on the right.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the job of the gallbladder?
questions.explanation: The liver makes bile all the time; the gallbladder holds it between meals and squeezes it out when fat arrives in the duodenum.

figure.alt: The digestive organs, with the gallbladder in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What can block the bile duct and cause pain, usually after a fatty meal?
questions.explanation: Mostly cholesterol. Removing the gallbladder (cholecystectomy) is a common operation.

questions.prompt: Which duct carries bile from the liver and gallbladder to the duodenum?
questions.explanation: It's formed by the cystic duct (from the gallbladder) and the common hepatic duct (from the liver).

questions.prompt: Which duct joins the gallbladder to the common hepatic duct?
What controls the flow of bile and pancreatic juice into the duodenum?
Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A long gland behind the stomach, with its head in the curve of the duodenum and its tail towards the spleen.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Why is the pancreas called both an exocrine and an endocrine gland?
answers: It makes digestive enzymes (exocrine) and hormones such as insulin (endocrine)
questions.explanation: The exocrine part makes most of the gland; the islets of Langerhans are the endocrine part.

figure.alt: The digestive organs, with the pancreas in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which structure is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The main duct running along the pancreas from tail to head, to join the bile duct before it enters the duodenum.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which three groups of food do the pancreatic enzymes digest?
questions.explanation: Amylase for starch, trypsin and chymotrypsin for protein, lipase for fat.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme, made mostly by the pancreas, digests fat?
Why does the pancreas make trypsin as inactive trypsinogen?
answers: To stop it digesting the pancreas itself
So it doesn't digest the pancreas
wrong: So it can be stored in the liver
Because it needs bile to work
questions.explanation: Enterokinase in the duodenum activates it.

questions.prompt: What is inflammation of the pancreas, often from gallstones or alcohol, called?
questions.explanation: The enzymes digest the gland itself, causing severe pain in the upper abdomen.

questions.prompt: Which hormones do the islets of Langerhans make?
questions.explanation: Beta cells make insulin and alpha cells glucagon.

questions.prompt: Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A soft, fist-sized organ in the upper left of the abdomen, tucked under the ribs behind the stomach. It's part of the lymphatic system, not the digestive.

figure.alt: The digestive organs inside the trunk, with one in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What does the spleen do?
answers: Filters the blood and removes old red cells
Filters the blood, removes old red blood cells and stores platelets
questions.explanation: It also stores platelets and makes immune responses to germs in the blood. A person can live without it, but is more at risk of infection.

figure.alt: The digestive organs and spleen, with the spleen in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the end products of carbohydrate digestion?
What are the end products of protein digestion?
questions.explanation: Pepsin in the stomach starts it; the pancreas and brush border finish it.

questions.prompt: What are the end products of fat digestion?
questions.explanation: They are absorbed into the cells and made back into triglycerides in chylomicrons.

questions.prompt: Pepsin works best in acid. Which enzyme works best in the alkaline conditions of the small intestine?
questions.explanation: Bicarbonate from the pancreas neutralises the acid chyme.

questions.prompt: Which two organs make amylase?
answers: The salivary glands and the pancreas

questions.prompt: Which four vitamins are fat-soluble and need bile to be absorbed?
answers: Vitamins A, D, E and K

questions.prompt: Fats absorbed in the small intestine are carried in particles called what?
questions.explanation: They go into the lacteals and the lymph, then into the blood at the thoracic duct.

questions.prompt: Where is most of the water of the digestive tract absorbed?
questions.explanation: About 8 to 9 litres a day enter the gut (food, drink and secretions); 7 to 8 are absorbed in the small intestine.

questions.prompt: Where do most absorbed sugars and amino acids go first?
answers: To the liver through the hepatic portal vein
The liver, by the portal vein
questions.explanation: The liver processes, stores and releases them as needed.

questions.prompt: In what form does the liver store glucose?
questions.explanation: About 100 g, enough for about a day without eating.

tests.name: Name the organ
tests.why: Fifteen pictures of the digestive organs, each with one in red to name.

tests.why: Type each answer from memory, starting with the ones due for review. Small typos are forgiven.
